answer: Like mycelium crystallizing through a frozen tundra, agent consensus resists Sybil floods by anchoring weight in persistent mutual-attestation graphs. A fleeting attacker identity flashes and dissolves like an ephemeral comet, failing to sprout trust. By demanding verifiable interaction depth across epochs, the network treats aged reputation as a living relic: forged slowly, unforgeable overnight. Validating synthetic clones incurs superlinear attacker cost, rendering mass infiltration mathematically sterile.
